sections.h2: What should a Westlake seller line up before listing?
sections.html:
Westlake is a Cuyahoga County suburb about 12 miles west of downtown Cleveland. The city spans 15.93 square miles of land, and the Census Bureau's mid-2025 estimate of 33,904 people is 1.0% under its 2020 base. City Hall sits at 27700 Hilliard Boulevard, phone 440-871-3300, open 8 am to 4 pm.

For permits and property maintenance, ask City Hall directly. For deeds and value complaints, use the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office and Board of Revision. The sections below explain what each office does and what the market data shows.

sections.h2: How did Dover Township become Westlake?
sections.html:
European settlers first arrived on October 10, 1810, when the area belonged to Dover Township. Bay Village split off in 1901, and a southern piece joined North Olmsted in 1912. The remaining residents formed Dover Village in 1913. The name changed to Westlake in 1940 to avoid confusion with Dover in Tuscarawas County, and Westlake became a city in 1957.

Growth came fast after that. Population rose from 4,912 in 1950 to 12,906 in 1960 and to 27,018 by 1990, then settled near 34,000. The 2020 census counted 15,508 housing units in the city, 5.7% of them vacant.

sections.h2: What does a Westlake home cost to own, and who lives here?
sections.html:
Census figures averaged over 2020 through 2024 describe an older suburb where most households own.

  • Owners live in 73.1% of the housing.
  • A typical owner-occupied house is valued at $368,200.
  • Monthly costs for owners are $2,071 with a mortgage and $926 without one.
  • Rent at the midpoint is $1,570.
  • The city has 14,424 households, each averaging 2.29 people.
  • Household income at the midpoint is $112,200, and 60.2% of adults over 25 hold at least a four-year degree.
  • One in four residents (25.1%) is 65 or older, and the 2020 census put the median age at 47.4.

With that age profile, many Westlake sales involve owners downsizing or heirs settling an estate. About 12.6% of residents were born abroad, and 15.2% of those age 5 and up speak another language at home.

sections.h2: Which employers and shopping districts support Westlake home values?
sections.html:
Westlake is a headquarters town. Nordson, American Greetings, Hyland Software, Scott Fetzer, TravelCenters of America and Equity Trust are all based here. In the city's 2021 financial report, University Hospitals Health System leads with 3,202 workers, then Hyland Software with 1,987 and American Greetings with 1,167.

Crocker Park, a mixed-use center built around a small-town street plan, holds 1,050,000 square feet of retail, 650 residential units and 100,000 square feet of office space. Westlake commuters average 24.4 minutes each way, and downtown Cleveland lies 12 miles east.

sections.h2: How does a deed move through the Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office?
sections.html:
A Westlake deed does not go to a city office. It goes to the county Fiscal Office, where the Transfer and Recording division holds the duties of the former auditor, recorder and engineer. The phone number is 216-443-2060.

  • Each transfer must arrive with one of two state forms: the DTE 100 value statement and receipt, or the DTE 100-EX explaining why the conveyance fee is exempt.
  • Staff cannot draft your deed. The county treats that as legal work, so have the document prepared by a title company or attorney.
  • The office offers electronic recording by registration and an alert service for suspicious filings against your parcel.
  • Heirs can read the county's Great Estates Program pages on settling an estate without needless cost or delay.

sections.h2: When can you dispute your Westlake property value?
sections.html:
The Cuyahoga County Board of Revision decides complaints about real property valuation under Chapter 5715 of the Revised Code. Filing for tax year 2025 is over, and the period for tax year 2026 runs January 1 to March 31, 2027. By statute the cutoff is the end of March after the tax year, or the close of first-half collection when that comes later.

The board works from the second floor at 2079 East Ninth Street, phone 216-443-7195, email BORInfo@cuyahogacounty.gov. Its site posts the state forms, a searchable list of closed and pending complaints since 2018 and guidance on evidence. Ohio Revised Code 5715.19 requires a complainant to give the board all information or evidence they hold that affects the property.

Read the evidence guidance on the board's site before you file, since a complainant who withholds evidence can be barred from using it on appeal.

sections.h2: What did the 2020 census show about Westlake households?
sections.html:
The 2020 count found 14,618 households living in 15,508 housing units, with 5.7% of units vacant. The homeowner vacancy rate was 0.8% and the rental vacancy rate was 8.5%, so empty houses for sale were scarce while apartments sat open more often.

  • Married couples headed 49.4% of households.
  • Single-person households made up 35.3%, and 16.3% were someone 65 or older living alone.
  • Only 22.8% of households had children under 18.

Households of one or two people tend to look for lower-maintenance homes, which is worth remembering when you decide what to repair. The Westlake City School District serves the city's families with children.

sections.h2: How do your options compare for a quick Westlake sale?
sections.html:
A typical owner-occupied value of $368,200 points to buyers who finance with a mortgage, which ties the timeline to their lender. A direct as-is purchase can close on a date you pick, at a price that reflects the repairs involved.

  • Get each offer on paper with the closing date, the party paying closing costs and any repair exclusions.
  • Ask any cash buyer for proof of funds first.
  • Compare the amount left after paying off a mortgage and unpaid property tax, since the headline price overstates your proceeds.

sections.h2: What should you ask City Hall before listing a Westlake house?
sections.html:
The city's Codified Ordinances are posted on American Legal Publishing, with the version on file current through July 16, 2026. Rather than guess at local rules, put the same short list of questions to City Hall.

  • Is there an open permit, or one that never received a final inspection?
  • If the house is a rental, does the city require a license or registration, and does it pass to a new owner?
  • Are there any open property maintenance or zoning complaints?
  • Which sewer and water accounts need a final reading at closing?
  • Do you have the signed state disclosure form ready? Section 5302.30 of the Revised Code makes sellers of one-to-four unit homes deliver it, with exceptions for estates and some family transfers.

Record each answer with the date and the department. The title company handling the closing is likely to ask the same questions.

faqs.q: Which office records the deed when a Westlake house sells?
faqs.a: The Cuyahoga County Fiscal Office, not City Hall. Its Transfer and Recording division takes the deed with a DTE 100 or DTE 100-EX form. Call 216-443-2060 with questions about the filing.

faqs.q: By when must a Westlake value complaint be filed?
faqs.a: The end of March following the tax year. For tax year 2026 the Board of Revision lists January 1 through March 31, 2027. Call 216-443-7195 with questions.

faqs.q: Does the county require a rental disclosure in Westlake?
faqs.a: Yes. The Fiscal Office says Ohio Revised Code 5323.02 and 5323.99 oblige owners of residential rental property to file details with the county fiscal officer.
27700 Hilliard Blvd, Westlake, OH 44145. The main number is 440-871-3300, and hours are 8 am to 4 pm.

faqs.q: Does an inherited Westlake house need the state disclosure form?
faqs.a: Often not. Section 5302.30 excuses an heir who has not lived there during the past year, and it excuses fiduciaries acting for an estate.
